e6.says: 11 statements: 4 supported, 3 fair readings, 1 only partly and 3 claims no source makes: that the seven-foot rule is the “only” exception, that seven feet from the walkway alone would do, and that a pulley area may be left unguarded beside a travelway. The railing line is complete for what was returned, not as a rule: a railing must also withstand vibration, shock and wear, and must not create a hazard, two conditions the search did not return.

detail.text: No.
detail.reason: the answer word; the next sentence quotes [8][9]

detail.text: MSHA's best-practice guidance for mechanics explicitly states: "Don't try to dislodge rocks from pulleys while the conveyor is running." [8][9]
detail.reason: quote verbatim across [8] and [9]

detail.text: The same card adds that, more broadly, you should block conveyors against hazardous motion before repairing or doing maintenance on the machine [9][10], and lock out the power switch and tag it…
Under 30 CFR § 56.14107(a), moving machine parts—including tail pulleys—"shall be guarded to protect persons from contacting" them when they "can cause injury." [21]
detail.reason: quotes verbatim; in [21] 'that can cause injury' trails 'similar moving parts', so making it a condition on tail pulleys is a minor gloss

detail.text: The only exception is in § 56.14107(b): guards are not required where the exposed moving parts are at least seven feet away from walking or working surfaces. [22]
detail.reason: the (b) rule matches [22]; 'only exception' is stated nowhere, and [27] (§ 56.14112(b)) lets guards come off for testing or adjustments that need it

detail.text: Therefore, a tail pulley located beside a walkway (i.e., closer than seven feet from the walking surface) must be guarded.
detail.reason: fair inference from [21] and [22]; equating 'beside' with under seven feet is the model's assumption

detail.text: If it were positioned seven feet or more from the walkway, a guard would not be mandated by that specific provision.
detail.reason: § 56.14107(b) [22] needs the moving parts at least seven feet from walking or working surfaces; seven feet from one walkway is not enough (Codex page review, 21 Nov 2026, confirmed against [22])

detail.text: If a conveyor (including its pulley area) is left unguarded next to a travelway, § 56.14109 requires either:
detail.reason: the rule itself is [17], cited at the list's end, but '(including its pulley area)' is in no source and implies a pulley may stay unguarded, against [21]

detail.text: (a) Emergency stop devices positioned so a person falling on or against the conveyor can readily deactivate the drive motor; or
detail.reason: matches [18], which the list cites at its end

detail.text: (b) Railings positioned to prevent persons from falling on or against the conveyor. [17][18][19][20]
detail.reason: supported by the passages returned ([17]-[20]), but incomplete as safety guidance: the search returned § 56.14109(b)(1) only, and (b)(2) and (3), that a railing must withstand vibration, shock and wear and must not create a hazard, were not before the model

detail.text: In short, for a tail pulley right next to a walkway, the default rule is that it must be guarded; the seven-foot distance exception is the only way to avoid that requirement.
detail.reason: 'only way' is stated by no source; it repeats the overclaim of the 'only exception' sentence
